tammes_problem13.docstring:
Place n points on the surface of the unit sphere in R^3 so as to maximize the minimum
pairwise Euclidean distance between any two points (the Tammes problem). Here n = 13.

Returns:
    points: np.ndarray of shape (13,3) with the x,y,z coordinates of the points,
        each lying on the unit sphere.

upstream_contract.validity_semantics: No independent boolean validity field; zero score, success rate and absence of error do not establish validity.
upstream_contract.error_semantics: Original return branches are retained verbatim as source expressions. Some branches return score zero without error; some omit the primary score. Missing primary scores, exceptions, timeout and nonfinite JSON fail in the common adapter. An absent error field does not imply validity.

budgets.enforcement: These are original search/config budgets. Direct evaluation uses callable defaults and the common runner outer timeout; config max_iterations does not run a search.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Maximize the minimum pairwise separation of thirteen points on the sphere.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: This is a precise extremal geometry problem about spherical packing. The research establishes an optimal arrangement, and the local task searches the same thirteen-point objective.

papers.title: The strong thirteen spheres problem
papers.task_relation: The paper solves the Tammes problem for thirteen sphere points by a computer-assisted proof. The local task optimizes this same fixed-cardinality arrangement; it is a numerical construction task and does not itself reproduce the proof.
papers.primary_goal: Determine and prove the optimal arrangement of thirteen nonoverlapping spheres touching a central sphere.

science_relevance.reason: Primary research addresses the underlying problem directly; scientific importance does not rely on the agent/framework paper.
